items.title: John Farnham’s Family Gives Rare Update on Legendary Singer’s Health
items.summary:
John Farnham ’s spirits remain high, his mind is sharp, but his body is failing. That’s the gist of a rare health update, shared from the legendary Australian singer’s family.

These days, the veteran singer is at home but gets around in a wheelchair and requires oxygen.

“His mental state is really good,” Rob Farnham, John’s son, told 102.5 ABC Perth Breakfast . “He’s spending a lot of time with his grandson whom he loves. He’s doing a lot of physical therapy. He’s happy, he’s laughing, he’s joking.”

John Farnham’s wife is a constant at his side. “Mum definitely sacrifices herself for dad and to help dad and she’s an amazing woman and we’re very proud of her as well,” Rob Farnham explains. “Obviously sometimes she gets a bit down but she has us to lean on and that’s what your family support is.”

The revered pop singer continues to stay out of the spotlight after undergoing marathon surgery in 2022 to remove a cancerous tumor from his throat. He will never sing again, his reps confirmed in May, but the time away from the public glare hasn’t dimmed his superstar status in these parts. 

Farnham was the focus of an all-star concert at Melbourne’s Rod Laver Arena on Sept. 20, featuring 120 artists and musicians, all of them selected by Farnham. The concert, a swift sellout, was cinecast into Hoyt’s theaters and served as a fundraiser for Head and Neck Cancer Australia . He was unable to attend, due to his condition. And when a jukebox musical based on Farnham’s career premiered recently in Sydney , he stayed away, which prompted the health update.

items.title: The month’s best folk album: Lizabett Russo confronts her roots on an odyssey through Transylvania
items.summary:
(Last Night from Glasgow)
Russo’s latest album Pe Unde Trece Dorul, roughly translated as Where Longing Goes, is full of surprises – and shows what a fantastically versatile singer she is

Long based in Scotland, Lizabett Russo returns to her native Romania for her fifth album of idiosyncratic, spectral folk. Having defied her parents’ wishes to leave the country age 18 and commence her musical journey, she travelled through Transylvania’s remote villages to learn doine (songs) and strigături (traditional rhymed shouts/calls), and named her album after a song taught to her by farmer Maria Dulău, a woman awarded a title to aim for by the Romanian National Institute of Heritage: Living Human Treasure. “Dorul” is like the Welsh hiraeth or Galician saudade, referencing longing and homesickness, and “trece” explains how these feelings travel, wander and pass.

Released by the label that also put out Dick Gaughan’s startling R/Evolution box set, Russo’s album begins like an update of Fourth World music created by trumpeter Jon Hassell and Brian Eno. A sly two-note guitar riff, Tim Lane’s soft drums, and Călin Han’s slowly blown kaval flutter coolness into the air, then Russo joins, multi-tracked and layered in harmony. Her voice is fantastically versatile: gentle yet agile on Bujori (Peonies), sprightly and knowing on Frumoasă-i Nevasta Ta Măi Ghită (Your…

items.title: ‘True Family’: Nile Rodgers Remembers Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor
items.summary:
You can’t choose you family. But you can choose your true family . That’s how Nile Rodgers remembers Andy Taylor , the founding guitarist of Duran Duran and The Power Station, who died this week following a years-long battle with prostate cancer, at the age of 65 .

Rodgers, like millions of music fans around the globe, is mourning the Englishman’s passing.

“Dear Andy Taylor RIP. How many countless great days and nights did we have?,” he writes. “I was sleeping last night when I heard the news of your passing. #RIP my dear friend. We were always happy when we were together. I love you.”

Rodgers and Taylor go way back. The Chic mainstay and elite record producer worked with Duran Duran on many of their hits, a friendship that began with the British new wave legends’ first U.S. No. 1 “The Reflex” from 1984.

Chic’s bass player Bernard Edwards produced the 1985 debut album from The Power Station, which gathered Duran Duran’s Andy and John Taylor, along with English singer Robert Palmer and U.S. drummer Tony Thompson. Rodgers provided some informal assistance to the project, which yielded the hits “Some Like It Hot” and a cover of Marc Bolan’s “Get It On (Bang A Gong)”.

“ #BernardEdwardsRIP loved you, and #TonyThompsonRIP loved you,” adds Rodgers, a cancer survivor. “Our two bands will be forever linked in the most special way. True family. Peace and eternal love.”

Rodgers shared a happy snap of himself with Andy, from somewhere, sometime in the 1980s, slapped with the caption: “The way I’ll always think of us…guitarist brothers.”

items.title: ‘We had a drug dealer called Satan on our tour bus’: Britpop stars Echobelly on debauchery, being pals with Oasis – and their spiritual return
items.summary:
They weathered excess, illness and being dropped and defrauded, but Echobelly are happily back as a duo. Ahead of a new album, they recall the weird fans and cliquey bands of the 90s

In 1994, Oasis toured the US for the first time, and a legend quickly emerged: these were Britain’s latest rock’n’roll renegades, who went berserk on crystal meth before a Los Angeles gig and almost split up afterwards. But Sonya Madan remembers it differently. Her band Echobelly were also touring the US that year, and the two groups hung out backstage at each other’s gigs.

“I’m gonna blow a myth!” she hoots. “For me, half the stuff about Oasis was made up by their press people. The people around them were partying; everyone was, including us, but it wasn’t that much. Liam was such a sweetheart, I used to go drinking with Noel, we were all mates.”

items.title: Soundtrack Of My Life: Serge Pizzorno
items.summary:
The first song I remember hearing 
 Chuck Berry – ‘Johnny B. Goode’ 

“Growing up, cartoons were massive. Looney Tunes , Tom And Jerry , [anything by] Hanna-Barbera. I love that period of 100-piece orchestras [making music] for a cartoon. Officially, if you’re thinking about the first music that was really impactful, it would be those kinds of songs, especially the Looney Tunes song [‘The Merry-Go-Round Broke Down’].

“But if I was to choose a more traditional song, ‘Johnny B. Goode’ will always probably remain the ‘Oh, that’s a song’ [moment]. My dad was really into the blues, Chuck Berry and John Lee Hooker. There’s something about the feel of that song that’s just ingrained. I’ve still never learnt it. I can play the rhythm guitar, but the solo’s not for me.”

The first album I ever owned 
 Michael Jackson – ‘Bad’ 

“Again, this is a long-ass time ago, so it could have been some mad A-Team  or [1985 sci-fi series] Street Hawk cassette – they used to bring mad albums out. But in terms of an actual studio album, it would have been Jacko’s ‘Bad’. I’ve got a crate of records that I brought from home in the attic. It will be there, somewhere. Pristine…”

The first gig I went to 
 Oasis and The Verve, Earl’s Court, September 1997 

“What a baptism of fire! I missed the local gigs and went straight in. Me and my pal, we had absolutely no idea what we’d got ourselves in for. They [opened with] ‘Be Here Now’, we separated and didn’t see each other again until the end of the gig. There were no phones, we lost all our dough. We were so thirsty, we had to drink tap water out of the…

items.title: 2027 BRIT Awards Trophy Designed by ‘One of Britain’s Greatest Living Artists’: See Photos
items.summary:
The 2027 BRIT Awards trophy has been designed by former Turner Prize-winning visual artist Dame Rachel Whiteread (Nov. 27).

Each year a different designer shapes a distinct creative vision for their trophy, modeled on the image of Britannia, traditionally represented by a female warrior with a shield and helmet.

In recent years, the trophy has been designed by iconic names such as Dame Vivienne Westwood, Sir Peter Blake, Tracey Emin, Dame Zaha Hadid, and last year’s designer, Matthew Williamson.

Whiteread took on 2027’s assignment, and her trophy will be presented to winners at the ceremony on Feb. 27 at the Co-op Live in Manchester.

In 1993, Whiteread became the first woman to win the Turner Prize, an accolade presented annually to a British visual artist; previous victors include Damien Hirst, Gilbert & George, and Anish Kapoor. Four years after her win, in 1997, she was the first woman to represent Britain at the Venice Biennale.

Her work primarily focuses on casting, and her Turner Prize-winning exhibit House (1993) featured a life-sized concrete cast of a Victorian terraced house in east London. Whiteread’s work has been exhibited in the Tate Museum, Paris’ Centre Pompidou and New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Museum of Modern Art.

Whiteread’s vision for the 2027 trophy features a steely, silver frame with holes punctuated throughout a silver frame alongside holes. “I used the motif of the BRIT Award and tried to change it in some way,” she said in a statement. “I exposed the interior of the statue – as an artist would do with their music.”

items.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Soundtrack Drives to No. 1 on ARIA Chart
items.summary:
There’s no stopping the Grand Theft Auto VI (via Atlantic/Warner) soundtrack, as it motors to No. 1 on the ARIA Albums Chart .

Spanning 34 tracks, including songs by Dua Lipa, Justice, Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen and more, GTA is the first soundtrack to top the national albums tally in 2026.

Meanwhile, its focus track “Flower In A Hurricane” (Ed Banger/Universal) by Justice, Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard And The Lizard Wizard roars 17-5 on the national singles chart, for Tame Impala’s third top 10 this year following “Dracula” and “Loser,” and marking a first-ever appearance in the top 50 for King Gizzard and Justice.

Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest video game drop of the year, or any year , raking in almost $4 billion globally on its first day of release.

Following the release of the deluxe version of Daughter From Hell (Interscope/Universal), featuring four new tracks, Gracie Abrams ’ third album bounces 26-6. Daughter From Hell logged one week at No. 1 in late July, for her second leader after 2024’s The Secret Of Us .

The all-star Forever Young (Virgin Music Group/Inertia) project from War Child Australia, the domestic arm of the international War Child organization, opens its account at No. 12. The fundraising collection houses songs by Paul Kelly, Missy Higgins, Ruel, Sarah Blasko, The Temper Trap, King Gizz, Grace Cummings, and a new, Paul Mac remix of Youth Group’s cover of Alphaville’s “Forever Young.” It’s the first ever benefit album for War Child Australia, with 100% of proceeds supporting children living through conflict.

items.title: Live Nation Adds Venue on Australia’s Gold Coast
items.summary:
GOLD COAST, Australia — Live Nation continues to expand its venues portfolio in Australia, adding a new facility on the Gold Coast.

Announced this week, Surfers Music Hall will be a 2,500-capacity live music space in Surfers Paradise, the hometown of chart-topping pop star Amy Shark , with a target to open its doors in mid-2028.

Surfers Music Hall will be the concerts giant’s first venue on the Gold Coast, and the first dedicated live music venue of this scale in the region. When complete, the space will bring more national and international tours to the Gold Coast, the second biggest city in Queensland, “while giving local artists a new stage,” reads a statement. Bookings will be open “to a range of promoters,” the message continues.

The timing of the new venue is critical. Queensland’s music and entertainment communities are preparing for the opportunity of a lifetime, when Brisbane hosts the 2032 Summer Olympic Games and Paralympic Games. The Gold Coast, about 50 miles south of Brisbane, won’t miss out. Hockey, triathlon, marathon swimming, and basketball games are earmarked for the city. 

The buzz is building for the local music scene, too, which has hosted concerts from the likes of Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters and Queen at Carrara Stadium. Also, Live Nation and the City of Gold Coast hosted a Ones to Watch showcase in 2022, and the 2026 Queensland Music Awards (QMAs) were presented on the Gold Coast for the first time in the event’s 20-year history.

items.title: Miranda Lambert Heats Up Halftime at Dallas Cowboys’ NFL Thanksgiving Game: Watch
items.summary:
Miranda Lambert gave Texans some homestyle country cooking Thursday night (Nov. 26), when she headlined the halftime spot in the NFL Thanksgiving contest between Dallas Cowboys and the visiting Philadelphia Eagles.

Wearing a black cowboy hat and a little black dress emblazoned with stars and finished with long, tasseled sleeves, Lambert delivered a nearly seven-minute medley — with support from the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, a full band and a strings section.

The three-time Grammy Award-winning star kicked things off with “Snakeskin Boots,” and got cooking with “Kerosene,” “Gunpowder & Lead,” “Mama’s Broken Heart,” and a cover of Audra Mae and The Almighty Sound’s “Little Red Wagon.”

“Happy Thanksgiving y’all, we love you Texas,” she said at the close.

Lambert has been on a tear of late. Just last week, she was the big winner at the 60th annual Country Music Awards, where she collected three trophies. With that hattrick, she lifted her career total of wins to 17, extending her lead as the female artist with the most victories.

The Longview, TX native ushered in her new album, Crisco , with a set Oct. 1 at the newly-opened Nashville venue The Truth, then dropped her Songline album on Nov. 13, followed by the companion film Songline on Nov. 20, both via Amazon Music. 

Also, Lambert co-wrote Ella Langley’ s Billboard Hot 100 smash hit “Choosin’ Texas,” which is now the longest-charting No. 1 in Hot 100 history, with 29 weeks atop the leaderboard. The Kansas City Chiefs will face the Buffalo Bills for the Thanksgiving Night game on Thursday, Nov. 26, at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York. The 5:20 p.m. PT/8:20 p.m. ET kickoff is the final game of the NFL’s Thanksgiving tripleheader, following the Chicago Bears vs. the Detroit Lions and the Philadelphia Eagles vs. the Dallas Cowboys earlier in the day. 

Local rock band Goo Goo Dolls , who hail from Buffalo, will provide the musical entertainment during halftime. Fans may also be watching for possible appearances by Taylor Swift , wife of Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, and Hailee Steinfeld, wife of Bills quarterback Josh Allen . The NFL game and music performance will air live on NBC and stream on Peacock. 

Since Peacock doesn’t offer a free trial of its own, we found several streaming services that do and include access to Peacock for free in their plans. items.title: Substance released at Don Toliver Co-Op live show could be linked to jewellery thefts and robberies, police say
items.summary:
Police have said that the “unknown substance” that led to a mass evacuation at a Don Toliver show in Manchester this week could be linked to jewellery thefts and robberies on the night.

READ MORE: Don Toliver – ‘Life Of A Don’ review: Texan rapper explores new depths 

Over 12,000 concertgoers were evacuated from Manchester’s Co-op Live arena on Sunday (November 22), after police declared a major incident at the venue shortly after 10pm. It was later confirmed that an “unknown substance”, initially believed to be tear gas, was released in the crowd, leading to some fans “screaming in pain”, “coughing up blood” and experiencing breathing difficulties (via BBC News ).

One person was taken to hospital and 88 others were treated at the scene. Greater Manchester Police have yet to identify the substance used, but have now shared that they have received nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert – believing that there may be a link between the gas being released and the thefts.

No arrests have been made at time of writing, and Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding has said that while the believe that there is “no wider ongoing risk” to the public at this time, there were similar reports made at previous Don Toliver shows in Europe.

“We are aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist,” he added, also saying that the police “will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending.”

An update from Co-op Live pic.twitter.com/9y9aWgkvwZ 

— Co-op Live…
items.t: Substance released at Don Toliver Co-Op live show could be linked to jewellery thefts and robberies, police say

items.title: Mwhahaha! After 50 years, the Damned are still an outrageously fun blast of punk, pop and gothic camp
items.summary:
Brighton Dome
Boasting all their surviving members, the quartet put on an extraordinarily eclectic and entertaining show, held together by pure ferocity

Few punk bands looked destined to make old bones – longevity wasn’t really the point – but you might have got particularly long odds on the Damned lasting any kind of distance. They were “the Bash Street Kids of punk”, in writer Jon Savage’s memorable estimation: “While other groups were carefully considering their moves,” he wrote, “the Damned went out there and pulled faces at the world as if there was no tomorrow.” Even their debut single New Rose implied they knew their time was limited: “I better go,” sang Dave Vanian amid its frantic thunder, “or it’ll be too late.”

How wrong can you be? Their peers are long gone or too riven by bad blood to work together, but the Damned are the one major punk band to observe the movement’s 50th anniversary with every surviving original member onstage, something you get the impression even the Damned are faintly startled by. “This is the kind of venue that would have told us to fuck off 50 years ago,” muses guitarist Captain Sensible, as he gazes around the Dome’s stately auditorium. Impressively, a substantial chunk of the audience respond by shouting “fuck off” in unison.

Continue reading...
items.t: Mwhahaha! After 50 years, the Damned are still an outrageously fun blast of punk, pop and gothic camp

items.title: a-ha’s Morten Harket: ‘My Parkinson’s diagnosis wasn’t devastating. I have a new appreciation for the human organism’
items.summary:
As the Norwegian pop trio’s frontman releases his new album Human Grace, he answers your questions on the devastating effects of fame, living in squalor in London, 80s nostalgia – and a certain bandmate’s denim underwear

You’ve described your new album, Human Grace, as revealing more of yourself than your previous work. Was there anything you found unexpectedly difficult to express through these songs, or anything that surprised you about yourself during the creative process? BarefootJax
No. It’s an exploratory process, the activity of making new music. It’s about quieting yourself, being available to hear tiny little differences in vibes, to pick up a seed that will blossom into something – and then it goes from being nothing to becoming a thing, instantaneously. That has never changed for me. With a-ha, there wasn’t much time and peace for songwriting. Being the frontman takes a lot of focus.

What has changed is my access to the skilled tools – singing and guitar – due to the Parkinson’s medication side-effects. For this album, we found old recordings of my voice, some from over 10 years back. It hasn’t been devastating for me to get this diagnosis – it has been a blunt and impactful instrument to stop everything I was doing. I had to reassemble myself first, to understand what it is. Losing access to parts of myself I’ve taken for granted all my life, but also a new appreciation for the architecture of ourselves as an organism – it’s so impressive. It’s…
items.t: a-ha’s Morten Harket: ‘My Parkinson’s diagnosis wasn’t devastating. I have a new appreciation for the human organism’

items.title: Bob Dylan review – at 85, he is in finer voice now than he was 40 years ago
items.summary:
Bournemouth International Centre
Kicking off yet another UK leg of his Never Ending Tour, Dylan may seem to treat his audience with indifference – but his songs are given imaginative, probing arrangements

Norman Mailer once asked whether a reader would finish The Old Man and the Sea if they did not already know Ernest Hemingway was the author. There are moments during this Bob Dylan set – the first of another UK leg of his so-called Never Ending Tour – where I wonder what we would make of tonight’s music if we were not aware of the identity of the now 85-year-old performer.

Ever since beginning the Never Ending Tour in the late 80s, Dylan has disdained crowd pleasing platitudes, preferring to reinterpret his vast oeuvre in his inimitable “late style”: the subdued jazz version of Tangled Up in Blue dropped halfway through the show is typical of his tendency to insulate old material in a new arrangement. Dylan’s decision to kick off these dates in Bournemouth at a time of year when the town’s wealthy snowbirds will have headed farther south, exhibits the same wilfulness, as does the very way he performs on stage. One can imagine Dylan rattling through tonight’s set even if the BIC were empty, a scenario completely congruous with his apparent indifference to the audience hellbent on deciphering his every syllable.

Continue reading...
items.t: Bob Dylan review – at 85, he is in finer voice now than he was 40 years ago

items.title: Novelist’s first album in eight years has Skepta, skits and soul – and showcases a true British original
items.summary:
(Mashwrks)
Sharp, unsentimental rhymes and a fearless disregard for genre make Scenes a richly varied victory lap for for one of grime’s most distinctive talents

It’s not often that a UK rap album arrives accompanied by its own air freshener and video game, but here we are. Head over to Novelist’s website, and you can find not merely the usual means of promoting a new release – branded hoodies, T-shirts and so on – but a scented mirror hanger that bears the album’s artwork and Scenes: the Drive, a vaguely Mario Kart-ish arcade game that involves driving around the landmarks of London and Los Angeles avoiding buses and the attentions of the traffic police to the strains of an album track called Prime.

But then, from the moment he appeared on the grime scene in his teens – so young he now constitutes an elder statesman in his late 20s – the south Londoner has cut something of a maverick figure in the world of UK rap. He arrived bearing a moniker that seemed oddly bookish among his more grittily named peers. His early releases saw him working alongside defiantly left-field producer Mumdance. He attracted a lot of press attention of the “grime’s brightest new hope” variety, but seemed to last about 20 minutes on the high-profile XL label before departing to start his own imprint, Mmmyeh.

items.title: ‘My brother was its first body’: would you add your corpse to Birkenhead’s pyramid of dead people?
items.summary:
Backed by the KLF, a monument is being built using 34,592 bricks, each containing a deceased person’s glazed ashes. Is this the future of funerals? We join emotional marchers on Birkenhead’s smoky, noisy Day of the Dead

Hundreds of people wearing hi-vis clothing are on a death march through Birkenhead Park. A burning shopping trolley leads the way, smoke grenades clog the air, and people holding traffic signs chant: “The dead don’t stop – till they reach the top.” There’s a wave of curtain-twitching from residents who look on with fear and bemusement as what looks like a psychedelic building site gone rogue marches through their beautiful recreation space. Where could they be going? The answer might shock some of them. For this crowd are on their way to build a pyramid … made of dead people.

“My brother calls it my ‘anarchist death cult,’” laughs Steve Lowe, chief engineer of L-13 Light Industrial Workshop, who is involved in running Birkenhead Day of the Dead and the People’s Pyramid. It’s an event that has taken place every year (except 2020) since 2018 in a variety of locations and was announced by Jimmy Cauty and Bill Drummond of the KLF (AKA the Justified Ancients of Mu Mu AKA K2 Plant Hire Ltd), the seminal electronic duo and experimental art provocateurs, when they returned after 23 years in 2017.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘My brother was its first body’: would you add your corpse to Birkenhead’s pyramid of dead people?

Justice bring some 80s nostalgia but this compilation of new material from music’s A-list – from Dua Lipa to Travis Scott and a host of Latin talent – stays at the cutting edge

It can be hard to ascertain why Grand Theft Auto VI is such a phenomenon from merely watching along with it. Equally devoted to the thrill of a violent crime story and a more mundane lifestyle fantasy, the appeal does not always translate to bystanders. Its soundtrack, however, is another story: a compilation of brand new material from some of the biggest pop, rap, rock and country artists on the planet – some of them combined in imaginative pileups of guest features – that can be enjoyed totally separately from the gameplay, if you so wish.

Starting from Zero, the opener by Justice – also composers of the game’s original score, released on 11 December – features the unmistakable voice of the Doobie Brothers’ Michael McDonald belting out an 80s-style pop ballad complete with a saxophone outro. This style is synonymous with Grand Theft Auto VI’s setting, a fictionalised version of Florida last seen in 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, which was beloved for its inclusion of 80s hits.

items.title: The Many Accomplishments Of DJ Python
items.summary:
Brian Piñeyro’s work is languid, yet he has a knack for chunky rhythm. As a teenager, he drummed in a marching ensemble and free jazz bands. He hoarded MP3s from blogs, purchased a Korg Electribe, and was gifted Technics by his best friend’s father. Relocating from Miami to Chicago for college, he frequented Gramaphone Records and Kstarke Records; spun at dives; and made beats as DJ Wey. Upon moving to New York City, he flirted with monikers, including Luis and Deejay Xanax, before forging a career as DJ Python.

The post The Many Accomplishments Of DJ Python appeared first on Stereogum .

items.title: ‘My name was poison’: Donny Osmond on fame, failure – and his friend Michael Jackson
items.summary:
He was the child star of the Osmonds who become a global celebrity by 14. Then, at 21, his career came crashing down. Here, he reveals how he survived his years in exile – and what happened when Jackson was accused of child abuse

For a brief period in the early 1970s, Donny Osmond ruled the world. He was the global teenage heart-throb. Even Michael Jackson trailed behind him. He was 14 when his most famous song, Puppy Love, spent five weeks at No 1 in the UK. My sister had a huge poster of him on her bedroom wall. Then again, everybody’s sister had a poster of him on their bedroom wall. Between 1972 and 1973 he had six Top 5 hits in the UK, three of them No 1s (including The Twelfth of Never and Young Love). He was equally successful back home in the US.

Osmond was clean-cut, religious and respectful, with a mighty ability to punch out cover versions of saccharine standards. From his purple velvet cap to his doleful eyes and dazzling all-American smile, he was a marketing dream. We’d only just finished with Beatlemania. And now there was Donnymania.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘My name was poison’: Donny Osmond on fame, failure – and his friend Michael Jackson

items.title: Interpol and Bloc Party review – two of 00s indie’s most revered acts go toe-to-toe
items.summary:
Utilita Arena Cardiff
Kele Okereke has a tough challenge selling Bloc Party’s trite latest album – a far cry from Interpol’s ‘masterpiece’ eighth record, performed here to darkly hypnotic effect

Try as one might to resist comparison, the balance of this particular yin and yang has been shifting for some time. Twelve months ago, when Interpol and Bloc Party announced a UK and European co-headline tour, the pairing looked like an even contest: two of 00s indie’s most revered acts, whose landmark debuts remain touchstones of the era.

Since then, their fortunes have diverged. As an opening bass drone strafes the room, Bloc Party arrive in Cardiff in superficially fine, if puzzling, form. Their seventh album, Anatomy of a Brief Romance, has been met with diminishing returns, its Snapchat-caption triteness – “Every day is such a vibe”, runs one refrain – and creative inertia doing little to win over listeners.

Continue reading...
items.t: Interpol and Bloc Party review – two of 00s indie’s most revered acts go toe-to-toe

items.title: ‘I do a really good version of AC/DC’s Highway to Hell, which throws people’: Sharleen Spiteri’s honest playlist
items.summary:
The Texas singer was fascinated by Elvis Costello as a kid and admires Nancy Sinatra’s sass and strength, but which of her own songs changed her life?

The first song I fell in love with
My mum gave me an old Dansette record player and a pile of albums. I must have been eight or 10, with my younger sister Corinne, getting butterflies to These Boots Are Made for Walkin’ by Nancy Sinatra. Years later, I read that she was told to sing it with a much more provocative attitude. You can hear the sass and the strength. Maybe that’s where my whole “don’t fuck with me” thing came from.

The song I do at karaoke
Give me any Marvin Gaye song, like You’re All I Need to Get By, and I’m all over it, but I’d normally pull someone up to duet with me.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘I do a really good version of AC/DC’s Highway to Hell, which throws people’: Sharleen Spiteri’s honest playlist
